records.source: נָ֣סוּ וְאֵין־רֹדֵ֣ף רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים כִּכְפִ֥יר יִבְטָֽח׃
records.gloss: They flee, and there is no one pursuing, [the] wicked; and [the] righteous like a young lion is confident.
pieces: The wicked run away when nobody is chasing them, \q but the righteous stand as bold as a lion.

L.1: [The] wicked flee when no one pursues, \q but [the] righteous [are] confident like a young lion.

R.1: Evil people run away even when no one is after them. \q But people who do right are brave, like a lion.

decisions.choice: flee when no one pursues: a guilty conscience
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and "wicked" singular: the wicked as a class take flight. Their own guilt chases them, as Leviticus 26:17, 36 warns.

decisions.choice: confident like a young lion: secure, unafraid
decisions.reason: The verb (batah) is to feel safe and trust. The young lion (kephir) is strong and fears no one (30:30).

records.source: בְּפֶ֣שַֽׁע אֶ֭רֶץ רַבִּ֣ים שָׂרֶ֑יהָ וּבְאָדָ֥ם מֵבִ֥ין יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ כֵּ֣ן יַאֲרִֽיךְ׃
records.gloss: By [the] transgression of a land many [are] its princes, and by a person [who] understands, knows, so it will last long.
pieces: When a land rebels, it has one ruler after another, \q but a person of understanding and knowledge keeps order lasting.

L.2: By [the] transgression of a land, its rulers [are] many, \q but by a person [who] understands [and] knows, \q [its] stability will last long.

R.2: When a country turns to wrongdoing, its leaders keep changing. \q But a wise leader who knows what is right helps the country stay strong for a long time.

decisions.choice: many rulers: rapid turnover of rulers
decisions.reason: A land given to rebellion (pesha) suffers rulers who rise and fall in quick succession, as in the northern kingdom (1 Kings 16:8–28).

decisions.choice: so it will last long: the land's stability endures
decisions.reason: The word ken can mean "so, thus" or "right, firm", and the subject of "will last long" is not named. The line most likely means that one person of understanding keeps the order of the land standing. The Greek translation reads the verse quite differently.

decisions.choice: a wise leader
decisions.reason: Readable names the person as a leader, since the contrast is with the many rulers of the first line.

records.source: גֶּ֣בֶר רָ֭שׁ וְעֹשֵׁ֣ק דַּלִּ֑ים מָטָ֥ר סֹ֝חֵ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: A man poor and oppressing poor [people] [is] a rain sweeping away, and there is no food.
pieces: A poor man who exploits the poor \q is like a beating rain that leaves no crops behind.

L.3: A poor man who oppresses [the] poor [is] a driving rain, \q and [there is] no food.

R.3: When a poor person cheats other poor people, it is like a heavy storm that washes away the crops. \q Nothing is left to eat.

decisions.choice: a poor man: one who is himself poor
alternatives: a ruler or head (rosh), by a change of vowels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads rash, "poor". It is surprising that a poor man should oppress the poor, and some read rosh, "head, ruler", with the Greek "bold man" behind it. The Hebrew as it stands makes a sharp point: the one who should know the hardship becomes its cause.

decisions.choice: a driving rain: a flood that ruins the crop
decisions.reason: Rain should bring food; this rain beats the grain flat and washes it away. Compare the kind rain of a good king in 16:15.

records.source: עֹזְבֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָה יְהַֽלְל֣וּ רָשָׁ֑ע וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י ת֝וֹרָ֗ה יִתְגָּ֥רוּ בָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: [Those who] forsake [the] law praise [the] wicked, and [those who] keep [the] law strive with them.
pieces: People who abandon God's instruction speak well of the wicked, \q but those who keep it stand up against them.

L.4: [Those who] forsake [the] law praise [the] wicked, \q but [those who] keep [the] law fight against them.

R.4: People who turn away from God's teaching say good things about evil people. \q But people who obey God's teaching stand against evil people.

decisions.choice: law: God's instruction (torah)
decisions.reason: The word torah means instruction; in Proverbs it can be a parent's teaching (1:8; 3:1). Here, and in verses 7 and 9, it stands as a standard by which the wicked and the righteous are told apart, which points to God's instruction (29:18).

decisions.choice: fight against them: oppose the wicked
decisions.reason: The verb (garah, hitpael) is to engage in strife. Those who keep the law do not approve the wicked but resist them.

decisions.choice: God's instruction
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the source, as at 29:18.

records.source: אַנְשֵׁי־רָ֭ע לֹא־יָבִ֣ינוּ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָבִ֥ינוּ כֹֽל׃
records.gloss: Men of evil do not understand justice, and [those who] seek YHWH understand everything.
pieces: Evil people cannot grasp what justice is, \q but those who seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} understand it fully.

L.5: Evil people do not understand justice, \q but [those who] seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} understand everything.

R.5: Evil people do not understand what is fair. \q But people who look to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} understand it completely.

decisions.choice: understand everything: understand justice in full
decisions.reason: In the parallel, "everything" (kol) answers "justice": those who seek the LORD see what is right in every case. It is not a promise of knowledge about all things. Compare 2:6–9; 1 Corinthians 2:15.

decisions.choice: understand it fully
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tie "everything" back to justice so it is not read as knowing all things.

records.source: טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם וְה֣וּא עָשִֽׁיר׃
records.gloss: Better [is] a poor [person] walking in his integrity than [one] crooked [of] two ways, and he [is] rich.
pieces: It is better to be poor and live with integrity \q than to be rich and two-faced in all you do.

L.6: Better [is] a poor [person] who walks in {{gender:their|his}} integrity \q than [one] crooked [in] two ways, even [if] rich.

R.6: It is better to be poor and honest than to be rich and dishonest.

decisions.choice: crooked in two ways: double-dealing
decisions.reason: The dual "two ways" pictures someone who goes one way in public and another in private (verse 18). The saying is close to 19:1, with "rich" in place of "fool".

records.source: נוֹצֵ֣ר תּ֭וֹרָה בֵּ֣ן מֵבִ֑ין וְרֹעֶה זֽ֝וֹלְלִ֗ים יַכְלִ֥ים אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: [One who] keeps [the] law [is] a son [who] understands, and a companion of gluttons shames his father.
pieces: A son who keeps instruction shows good sense, \q but one who runs with gluttons disgraces his father.

L.7: [One who] keeps instruction [is] an understanding son, \q but a companion of gluttons shames his father.

R.7: A son who obeys what he is taught is wise. \q But a son who spends his time with people who eat and drink too much brings shame to his father.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's law as taught by a father
decisions.reason: Torah here sits beside a son and his father, so it may be the father's teaching (1:8; 4:2). In this chapter (verses 4, 9) it is God's instruction, which a father passed on to his son (Deuteronomy 6:6–7); the two need not be separated.

decisions.choice: companion of gluttons: the rebellious son of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The word (zolel) describes the stubborn son of Deuteronomy 21:20, "a glutton and a drunkard". Compare 23:20–21.

records.source: מַרְבֶּ֣ה ה֭וֹנוֹ בְּנֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּ֑ית לְחוֹנֵ֖ן דַּלִּ֣ים יִקְבְּצֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: [One who] increases his wealth by interest and usury, for [one who] is gracious [to the] poor he gathers it.
pieces: Whoever grows rich by charging interest and taking a cut \q is only storing it up for someone who will be generous to the poor.

L.8: [Whoever] increases {{gender:their|his}} wealth by interest and profit \q gathers it for [one who] is kind [to the] poor.

R.8: Some people get rich by charging high interest. \q But in the end their money will go to someone who is kind to poor people.

decisions.choice: and profit, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written text has "by" before the second word; the scribes' reading has "and". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: interest and profit: charges on loans to the poor
decisions.reason: The Law forbade lending to a poor Israelite at interest (neshek) or for profit (tarbit) (Leviticus 25:36–37; Deuteronomy 23:19–20). Wealth gained this way passes in the end to the generous (13:22; Ecclesiastes 2:26).

records.source: מֵסִ֣יר אָ֭זְנוֹ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ תּוֹרָ֑ה גַּֽם־תְּ֝פִלָּת֗וֹ תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃
records.gloss: [One who] turns aside his ear from hearing [the] law, even his prayer [is] an abomination.
pieces: If anyone refuses to listen to God's instruction, \q even their prayer is detestable.

L.9: [Whoever] turns {{gender:their|his}} ear away from hearing [the] law, \q even {{gender:their|his}} prayer [is] an abomination.

R.9: If you will not listen to God's teaching, \q God hates even your prayers.

decisions.choice: even his prayer is an abomination: to God
decisions.reason: Compare 15:8, where the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD. Whoever will not hear God should not expect God to hear him (1:24–28; Isaiah 1:15; Zechariah 7:11–13).

decisions.choice: law: God's instruction (torah)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4; the link with prayer makes it God's instruction.

decisions.choice: God hates
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who finds such prayer detestable, which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: מַשְׁגֶּ֤ה יְשָׁרִ֨ים׀בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ רָ֗ע בִּשְׁחוּת֥וֹ הֽוּא־יִפּ֑וֹל וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִנְחֲלוּ־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: [One who] leads astray [the] upright in a way of evil, in his own pit he will fall, and [the] blameless will inherit good.
pieces: Whoever lures the upright into an evil path \q will fall into their own pit, \q but the blameless will receive good things.

L.10: [Whoever] leads [the] upright astray into an evil way \q will fall into {{gender:their|his}} own pit, \q but [the] blameless will inherit good.

R.10: If you lead good people into doing wrong, you will fall into your own trap. \q But people who do right will receive good things.

decisions.choice: falls into his own pit: the trap turns on its maker
decisions.reason: Compare 26:27; Psalm 7:16; Matthew 18:6.

records.source: חָכָ֣ם בְּ֭עֵינָיו אִ֣ישׁ עָשִׁ֑יר וְדַ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין יַחְקְרֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Wise in his own eyes [is] a man rich, and a poor [person] [who] understands searches him out.
pieces: The rich may think they are wise, \q but a poor person with insight sees right through them.

L.11: A rich person [is] wise in {{gender:their|his}} own eyes, \q but a poor [person who] has understanding sees through {{gender:them|him}}.

R.11: Rich people often think they are very wise. \q But a poor person who has good sense can see what they are really like.

decisions.choice: searches him out: tests and sees through him
decisions.reason: The verb (haqar) is to examine closely, as in 18:17 and 25:2. Wealth does not make wisdom, and the poor may see what the rich man cannot.

records.source: בַּעֲלֹ֣ץ צַ֭דִּיקִים רַבָּ֣ה תִפְאָ֑רֶת וּבְק֥וּם רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְחֻפַּ֥שׂ אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: When [the] righteous rejoice, great [is the] glory, and when [the] wicked rise, a person is searched for.
pieces: When the righteous win, there is great celebration, \q but when the wicked come to power, people go into hiding.

L.12: When [the] righteous triumph, great [is the] glory, \q but when [the] wicked rise, people hide themselves.

R.12: When good people win, everyone celebrates. \q But when evil people take power, people hide.

decisions.choice: a person is searched for: people hide and must be sought out
decisions.reason: The passive verb (hapas) means people have to be searched for, because they have gone into hiding. Verse 28 says it plainly with a different verb. Compare 11:10; 29:2.

decisions.choice: rejoice: triumph, exult in victory
decisions.reason: The verb (alats) is exultation, here at the success of the righteous, set against the wicked who "rise" to power.

records.source: מְכַסֶּ֣ה פְ֭שָׁעָיו לֹ֣א יַצְלִ֑יחַ וּמוֹדֶ֖ה וְעֹזֵ֣ב יְרֻחָֽם׃
records.gloss: [One who] covers his transgressions will not prosper, and [one who] confesses and forsakes [them] will be shown mercy.
pieces: Whoever hides their sins will not succeed, \q but whoever admits them and turns away from them will receive mercy.

L.13: [Whoever] conceals {{gender:their|his}} transgressions will not prosper, \q but [whoever] confesses and forsakes [them] will find mercy.

R.13: If you hide your sins, things will not go well for you. \q But if you admit them and stop doing them, God will show you mercy.

decisions.choice: conceal or confess
decisions.reason: Compare Psalm 32:3–5, where keeping silent wears the psalmist down and confession brings forgiveness, and 1 John 1:9. Mercy follows confession joined with forsaking the sin.

decisions.choice: will be shown mercy: by God
decisions.reason: The passive verb (raham) leaves the giver unnamed; in the light of the Psalm it is God's compassion.

decisions.choice: God will show you mercy
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who shows mercy, to avoid a passive.

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] a person [who] fears continually, and [one who] hardens his heart will fall into calamity.
pieces: How blessed is the one who is always reverent, \q but whoever hardens their heart will fall into disaster.

L.14: How blessed [is] a person who fears continually, \q but [whoever] hardens {{gender:their|his}} heart will fall into trouble.

R.14: People who always take God and sin seriously are truly happy. \q But people who make their hearts stubborn will end up in trouble.

decisions.choice: fears continually: lives in reverent caution
decisions.reason: The verb (pahad, piel) is to be in dread. It is not the usual word for the fear of the LORD, and the object is not named; it is a tender conscience that trembles before God and keeps away from sin, set against the hard heart. Compare Isaiah 66:2.

decisions.choice: hardens his heart
decisions.reason: The hard heart refuses God's warnings, like Pharaoh's (Exodus 7:13; Psalm 95:8).

decisions.choice: take God and sin seriously
decisions.reason: Readable names what the fear is directed toward, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: אֲרִי־נֹ֭הֵם וְדֹ֣ב שׁוֹקֵ֑ק מֹשֵׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע עַ֣ל עַם־דָּֽל׃
records.gloss: A lion roaring and a bear charging [is] a ruler wicked over a people poor.
pieces: Like a roaring lion or a bear on the attack \q is a wicked ruler over helpless people.

L.15: A roaring lion and a charging bear \q [is] a wicked ruler over a poor people.

R.15: A wicked ruler over poor people \q is as dangerous as a roaring lion or an attacking bear.

decisions.choice: charging bear: a bear rushing to attack
decisions.reason: The verb (shaqaq) is to run or rush about, like locusts (Isaiah 33:4). The poor have no defense against such a ruler. Compare 17:12; 19:12.

records.source: נָגִ֗יד חֲסַ֣ר תְּ֭בוּנוֹת וְרַ֥ב מַעֲשַׁקּ֑וֹת שֹׂ֥נֵא בֶ֝֗צַע יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: A leader lacking understanding and great [in] extortions; [one who] hates unjust gain will prolong days.
pieces: A ruler without sense is a harsh oppressor, \q but one who hates dishonest gain will reign long.

L.16: A ruler lacking understanding [is] also great [in] extortion, \q [but one who] hates unjust gain will prolong [his] days.

R.16: A ruler with no good sense takes things from people by force. \q But a ruler who hates getting money by cheating will rule for a long time.

decisions.choice: one who hates, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written text has a plural; the scribes' reading is singular. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a ruler lacking understanding is great in extortion
alternatives: a ruler lacking understanding and great in extortion (hates unjust gain, and so lives long)
decisions.reason: The first line has no verb. It is most likely a statement: a foolish ruler oppresses. The second line sets against it the ruler who hates unjust gain (1 Samuel 12:3–4).

records.source: אָ֭דָם עָשֻׁ֣ק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁעַד־בּ֥וֹר יָ֝נ֗וּס אַל־יִתְמְכוּ־בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A person burdened by [the] blood of a life, to [the] pit he will flee; let them not support him.
pieces: Someone tormented by guilt for shedding blood will be a fugitive until death; \q let no one stand in their way.

L.17: A person weighed down by [the] blood of a life will flee to [the] pit; \q let no one hold {{gender:them|him}} up.

R.17: A person who has murdered someone will run from guilt until death. \q Do not try to help or stop that person.

decisions.choice: burdened by the blood of a life: guilty of murder
alternatives: oppressed by the guilt of bloodshed
decisions.reason: The verb (ashaq) is usually to oppress; here the passive pictures someone weighed down by the guilt of taking a life (Genesis 4:12–14; Numbers 35:31).

decisions.choice: flee to the pit: be a fugitive until death
alternatives: flee to a pit for refuge
decisions.reason: The pit (bor) is the grave. The murderer runs from guilt and justice until he dies.

decisions.choice: let no one hold him up: neither help nor hinder
decisions.reason: The verb (tamak) is to grasp or support. It may forbid helping the murderer escape justice, or forbid holding him back from his flight to death. The verse is hard in every line.

decisions.choice: stand in their way; help or stop
decisions.reason: Balanced chooses one sense of the ambiguous verb; Readable keeps both.

records.source: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים יִוָּשֵׁ֑עַ וְנֶעְקַ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם יִפּ֥וֹל בְּאֶחָֽת׃
records.gloss: [One who] walks blameless will be delivered, and [one who is] crooked [of] two ways will fall at once.
pieces: Whoever lives with integrity will be kept safe, \q but anyone who is double-dealing will suddenly fall.

L.18: [Whoever] walks blameless will be saved, \q but [one who is] crooked [in] two ways will fall all at once.

R.18: People who live right will be kept safe. \q But people who are dishonest will fall all of a sudden.

decisions.choice: at once: suddenly
alternatives: in one of the two ways
into a pit (by a small change of letters)
decisions.reason: The phrase (be'ehat) can mean "at once, suddenly", or it may mean the crooked person falls in one of the two ways he tries to walk. Some, following the Syriac, read "into a pit".

decisions.choice: crooked in two ways: double-dealing
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֥ף רֵ֝קִ֗ים יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־רִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: [One who] works his land will be satisfied [with] bread, and [one who] pursues empty [things] will be satisfied [with] poverty.
pieces: Those who farm their land will have food in plenty, \q but those who chase fantasies will have poverty in plenty.

L.19: [Whoever] works {{gender:their|his}} land will have plenty [of] bread, \q but [whoever] chases worthless [things] will have plenty [of] poverty.

R.19: If you work hard on your farm, you will have plenty to eat. \q But if you chase after foolish dreams, you will end up very poor.

decisions.choice: almost the same as 12:11
decisions.reason: The first line repeats 12:11; the second ends with a play on the verb: one is filled with bread, the other filled with poverty.

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ אֱ֭מוּנוֹת רַב־בְּרָכ֑וֹת וְאָ֥ץ לְ֝הַעֲשִׁ֗יר לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
records.gloss: A man of faithfulness [will be] great [in] blessings, and [one] hastening to become rich will not go unpunished.
pieces: A faithful person will be richly blessed, \q but one who rushes to get rich will not escape punishment.

L.20: A faithful person [will have] many blessings, \q but [whoever] hurries to get rich will not go unpunished.

R.20: People who can be trusted will receive many blessings. \q But people who try to get rich quickly will be punished.

decisions.choice: a man of faithfulness: someone reliable and honest
decisions.reason: The plural (emunot) intensifies: a thoroughly trustworthy person, set against the one who will cut corners to get rich quickly (13:11; 20:21; 28:22).

records.source: הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֥ים לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְעַל־פַּת־לֶ֝֗חֶם יִפְשַׁע־גָּֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: To regard faces [is] not good, and for a piece of bread a man will transgress.
pieces: Favoritism is never right, \q yet some will do wrong for a mere scrap of bread.

L.21: Showing partiality [is] not good, \q yet for a piece of bread a man will do wrong.

R.21: It is wrong to treat some people better than others. \q But some people will do wrong for just a little food.

decisions.choice: regard faces: show partiality, especially in judgment
decisions.reason: To "recognize faces" is to favor someone for who they are (18:5; 24:23; Deuteronomy 1:17).

decisions.choice: for a piece of bread: for a trifling bribe
decisions.reason: The second line shows how cheaply judgment can be bought. Compare Ezekiel 13:19.

records.source: נִֽבֳהָ֥ל לַה֗וֹן אִ֭ישׁ רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝דַע כִּי־חֶ֥סֶר יְבֹאֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Hastening to wealth [is] a man evil of eye, and he does not know that want will come to him.
pieces: A stingy person is in a rush to get rich, \q not knowing that poverty is on its way.

L.22: A person [with an] evil eye hurries after wealth \q and does not know that want will come upon {{gender:them|him}}.

R.22: Greedy people hurry to get rich. \q They do not know that they will end up poor.

decisions.choice: evil of eye: stingy, greedy
decisions.reason: The "evil eye" is a grudging, greedy outlook, the opposite of the "good eye" of the generous in 22:9. Compare 23:6.

records.source: מ֘וֹכִ֤יחַ אָדָ֣ם אַ֭חֲרַי חֵ֣ן יִמְצָ֑א מִֽמַּחֲלִ֥יק לָשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: [One who] rebukes a person afterward will find favor more than [one who] makes smooth [the] tongue.
pieces: In the end, a person who corrects someone will be more appreciated \q than one who flatters.

L.23: [Whoever] rebukes a person will afterward find more favor \q than [one who] flatters with [the] tongue.

R.23: If you correct someone, later that person will thank you more \q than if you had only said nice things.

decisions.choice: afterward: in the end
decisions.reason: The word (aharay) is most likely "afterward": the rebuke stings at first, but later earns more gratitude than flattery. Compare 27:5–6; 29:5.

decisions.choice: makes the tongue smooth: flatters

records.source: גּוֹזֵ֤ל׀אָ֘בִ֤יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ וְאֹמֵ֥ר אֵֽין־פָּ֑שַׁע חָבֵ֥ר ה֝֗וּא לְאִ֣ישׁ מַשְׁחִֽית׃
records.gloss: [One who] robs his father and his mother and says, "[It is] not a transgression," [is] a companion of a man [who] destroys.
pieces: Whoever robs their father or mother \q and says, "There is nothing wrong with that," \q is no better than a vandal.

L.24: [Whoever] robs {{gender:their|his}} father or {{gender:their|his}} mother \q and says, "[It is] no wrong," \q [is] a companion to a destroyer.

R.24: Some people steal from their own parents and say, "That is not wrong." \q They are just as bad as someone who wrecks things.

decisions.choice: robbing father or mother
decisions.reason: Compare 19:26 and 20:20. A child who takes a parent's goods, perhaps by claiming an inheritance early, excuses it as no crime; Jesus condemns a similar evasion in Mark 7:10–13.

decisions.choice: companion of a destroyer: in league with those who ruin
decisions.reason: Compare 18:9, where the slack worker is "brother to a destroyer".

records.source: רְחַב־נֶ֭פֶשׁ יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ עַל־יְהוָ֣ה יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃
records.gloss: [One] wide of soul stirs up strife, and [one who] trusts in YHWH will be made fat.
pieces: Greedy people stir up conflict, \q but whoever trusts in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will prosper.

L.25: A greedy person stirs up strife, \q but [whoever] trusts in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be enriched.

R.25: Greedy people start fights. \q But people who trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will have more than enough.

decisions.choice: wide of soul: greedy, with an appetite that is never full
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures an appetite opened wide (Habakkuk 2:5). Some take it as pride; set against trust in the LORD, it is the grasping self-reliance that causes quarrels.

decisions.choice: made fat: prosperous, well provided
decisions.reason: As in 11:25 and 13:4; compare 29:25.

records.source: בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭לִבּוֹ ה֣וּא כְסִ֑יל וְהוֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּ֝חָכְמָ֗ה ה֣וּא יִמָּלֵֽט׃
records.gloss: [One who] trusts in his own heart, he [is] a fool, and [one who] walks in wisdom, he will be delivered.
pieces: Whoever trusts their own mind is a fool, \q but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.

L.26: [Whoever] trusts in {{gender:their|his}} own heart [is] a fool, \q but [whoever] walks in wisdom will escape.

R.26: If you trust only your own ideas, you are a fool. \q But if you live wisely, you will be safe.

decisions.choice: his own heart: his own mind and judgment
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thinking and choosing. Trusting one's own judgment is set against trusting the LORD (verse 25; 3:5).

records.source: נוֹתֵ֣ן לָ֭רָשׁ אֵ֣ין מַחְס֑וֹר וּמַעְלִ֥ים עֵ֝ינָ֗יו רַב־מְאֵרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: [One who] gives to [the] poor, there is no lack, and [one who] hides his eyes [will be] great [in] curses.
pieces: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, \q but whoever looks away from them will receive many curses.

L.27: [Whoever] gives to [the] poor [will have] no lack, \q but [whoever] hides {{gender:their|his}} eyes [will have] many curses.

R.27: If you give to poor people, you will have all you need. \q But if you ignore them, many people will curse you.

decisions.choice: hides his eyes: refuses to see the need
decisions.reason: To hide the eyes is to look away deliberately (Isaiah 1:15; compare Deuteronomy 15:7–11). The curses may come from the poor themselves (11:26).

records.source: בְּק֣וּם רְ֭שָׁעִים יִסָּתֵ֣ר אָדָ֑ם וּ֝בְאָבְדָ֗ם יִרְבּ֥וּ צַדִּיקִֽים׃
records.gloss: When [the] wicked rise, a person hides, and when they perish, [the] righteous increase.
pieces: When the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding, \q but when the wicked are destroyed, the righteous flourish.

L.28: When [the] wicked rise, people hide themselves, \q but when they perish, [the] righteous increase.

R.28: When evil people take power, everyone hides. \q But when evil people die, there are more and more good people.

decisions.choice: people hide, the righteous increase
decisions.reason: This repeats the theme of verse 12 and is taken up again in 29:2, 16.
